restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1: SHA-256 compression steps 0..30 inclusive on every padded block, standard fixed IV once at the start, FIPS 180-4 padding, full feed-forward, full 256-bit big-endian digest; ordinary collision of two distinct finite byte strings.

The online attack is a SINGLE-SEED CAPPED search, not a replay and not an until-success loop: one seed s (SHA-256-derived from the committed root string plus an index, fixed before any solve) drives the r31k K-scan for AT MOST T = 64,117,538,956 = ceil(2^35.90) independent trials. Each trial runs the shared-prefix partial compression for steps 15..30 of one 512-bit block under a fixed 15-step prefix (one full 31-step compression's worth of word operations plus at most 256 further ops including one bitmap probe: shift + byte index + bit test), then a deterministic FAIL branch. No unbounded retry-until-success construct exists; the worst-case online instruction count is the fixed number in proof.md Sections 4-5.

EXPECTATION ACCOUNTING, fully disclosed: the charged trial term is T x 1.119897 units/draw. The per-draw rate 1.119897 = (C+256)/C for the trial itself plus amortized per-hit stages (31-step re-compression on bitmap hit, record-bucket walk, v6/rho stages, group prefix) at the WORST measured per-draw mix across the five sampling runs (proof.md Section 4-5). All five measured first-collision trial counts n* are disclosed: 3,252,363,302 / 3,331,059,371 / 63,747,366,391 / 85,779,856,984 / 171,274,355,349 (log2 31.599 / 31.633 / 35.892 / 36.320 / 37.318). The claim prices the distribution's CENTRAL expectation (sample median 2^35.8916; the alternative central reading sample mean 2^35.9303 moves the total to 2^36.656, above the 4-decimal claim — the median is the claimed central reading), not the best draw.

success_probability = 0.5 is the median-definition floor, not model confidence: under the single score-critical heuristic H-MEDIAN (proof.md Section 9), the population median m of n* over fresh seeds satisfies m <= 2^35.90, hence P[n* <= T] >= 0.5 by definition of a median, and 0.5 >= 0.39 with 0.11 absolute margin. The estimate m <= 2^35.90 rests on five pre-committed independent seeds with sample median 2^35.8916 and mean 2^35.9303; three of five draws lie at or below T. Binomial weight disclosed: if m > T, P[>=3 of 5 draws <= T] = 0.5, so the sample is consistent with the premise, not a proof of it.

COMPLETE LEDGER (proof.md Section 7, exact rationals): total = 1.1 x (set-scan 1,874,178,103.6 + z3 solve 22,165,546,530.6 + table build 81,051,258.5 + tooling/lab 1,001,000,000 + trial term 71,805,017,397.5) = 106,619,472,619.19 units = 2^36.6337, claimed as time_log2 36.6337, the tightest holding 4-decimal value, with the integer-power both-directions check 2^36.6336 x D^10000 < N^10000 <= 2^36.6337 x D^10000 in Section 7. Every executed run in the chain that PRODUCED this construction is charged once: the r31sets enumeration scan, the single z3 4.15.1 solve (seed 1547760900, SAT on first sequential attempt), one table build, scripting, plus 10% margin. The five sampling K-runs are construction VALIDATION of the n* distribution, disclosed separately in Section 8.

preprocessing_log2 = 34.69 has its OWN ledger, not a copy of the total: 1.1 x (1,874,178,103.6 + 22,165,546,530.6 + 81,051,258.5 + 1,001,000,000) = 27,633,953,481.97 = 2^34.6857 < 34.69 - the one-time construction part (scan + solve + build + tooling) that preprocessing subsumes inside the total. Nonuniform advice (declared 2^12 bytes) is the target-specific constants only: the five 13-word starting-solution arrays and W9' word (264 B) and the relaxed-condition delta/mask constants (~36 B) baked into the scan program, plus the 1,920 B witness blocks embedded as hex constants in the replay experiment (~2.3 KiB total); the 2^20-row record table and 2^21-byte bitmap are rebuilt inside charged time and are not advice. FIPS 180-4 round constants and the standard IV are target-spec code, not advice.

Memory is a reported metric only (no scalar contribution, no tie-break, not a declared heuristic). Peak measured is the instrumented z3 solve at 219,676,672 B = 2^27.71 (rusage maxrss, tl-1547760900.log); memory_log2_bytes = 28 covers it with margin. The r31k scan peaks near 2^24.7 B: 24 B x 2^20 record rows + 2^21 B bitmap + static V7/V8/cts arrays + code.

Certificates are the five measured 128-byte two-block collision pairs shipped as binary files; the organizer verifies message distinctness and full 31-step digest equality independently. The shipped experiment replays the same five pairs from embedded constants (the sandbox mounts only the program file; no sibling opens) and evidences the collision RELATION only - it executes no search and no cost or frequency is inferred from it. baseline_improved = sha256-r31-nominal-v2 is a required reference identifier and asserts no improvement.

heuristics.statement: For the r31k K-scan on a FRESH SHA-derived seed, the population median m of the first-collision trial count n* satisfies m <= 2^35.90. Then P[success within T = ceil(2^35.90) trials] >= 0.5 by the definition of the median, meeting the 0.39 floor with margin 0.11. Support: five pre-committed independent seeds gave n* log2 values 31.599, 31.633, 35.892, 36.320, 37.318 - sample median 2^35.8916 <= 2^35.90 and sample mean 2^35.9303; three of five draws at or below T.
heuristics.scope: Applied only to the per-seed first-collision trial-count distribution of the exact r31k construction (own starting solution seed 1547760900, relaxed-cancellation W20 context, 2^20-row record table + 2^21-byte bitmap over key>>8) over fresh uniform seeds, priced in the measured worst per-draw mix. It prices EXPECTED search work of one capped single-seed run. It is not a claim that SHA-256-r31 is ideal and not a worst-seed claim; the TIME bound does not depend on it (the time bound is the program's own capped operation count at the measured worst rate).
heuristics.extrapolation: n* is a first-hit count of a geometric-like process; the per-trial pass rate implied by the five measured draws is 2^-35.90 to 2^-37.32, consistent stage-by-stage with the enumerated hit chain (key-hit 2^-17.5, v6 retention 2^-8.96, r20 pick 1/3087, one completion). Sensitivity: sample-mean pricing moves the total 2^36.6337 -> 2^36.6560 (above the 4-decimal claim; the claim deliberately prices the median reading); pricing the 4th order statistic (2^36.320) gives 2^36.956 and the max draw (2^37.318) gives 2^37.796 - both disclosed pessimistic readings in Section 8, the second above the pending head, which is exactly why the claim says median, not worst-case.
heuristics.limitations: Five samples estimate the median; the binomial evidence is weak by construction (under m > T the chance of >=3 of 5 draws <= T is at most 0.5; under m = 2^36.32 a geometric-median model gives p = 0.40 and that chance 0.32, so the observed 3/5 is more consistent with m <= 2^35.90 than with m at the 4th order statistic). If the panel rejects median-expectation pricing for a randomized search and demands all executed sampling work, the honestly repriced claim is 2^38.67 and this ticket should be refuted rather than reinterpreted. The tail of n* beyond 2^37.32 is unmeasured: sampling runs stopped at first collision by design, so no draw above the max was observed.
